title: Stonemouth — where the Ferr comes down to the Ilm
caption: The quarry village five leagues upriver of Sill, drawn at walking scale where the Ferr comes down to the Ilm: the sandstone workings and the lime yard on the rising bank, the lime kilns with their smoke, the ale-room beside the kiln, the village houses, and the weigh-clerk's bench by the landing with punts on the river. The river road runs east to Sill and west over the ford to Nine Pots three leagues away; the Lead Run comes in from the west stained blue-grey from an old working, and the Rim Road passes north-west toward Keld Keep. Sill and Nine Pots are drawn faint at the edges for neighbourhood only. Cartouche dated Y.H. 813, the month of Grain, with compass, a league scale in paces, a convention of signs and surveyor's notes on the lime, sandstone and reed-wolf tooth that go out by water, the Ferr that makes a man thin with no figure set against it, the thirty-year habit of stopping at the end of the part when a clean coat comes up from Greybank, and the name kept in a room against the name kept on a slate. An engraved reed-wolf tooth sits in the margin.
